pairs.statement: The specialised commercial court hears intellectual property, commercial company, judicial settlement and bankruptcy, bank and financial institution disputes with traders, maritime, air transport and commercial insurance, and international trade disputes.

Before a claim in which specialised commercial matter is one of intellectual_property, commercial_company, bankruptcy_settlement, bank_with_merchant, maritime_air_insurance, international_trade, a conciliation attempt must have taken place, except when: The specialised commercial court's jurisdiction rules apply only from its installation, and the commercial section stays competent until then; the prior conciliation is a step before that court. This is a reading the text does not settle, so boundary n7 warns in this case; Paragraph 3 of article 536 مكرر 4 calls for the record of non-conciliation in case the attempt fails; where it ended in a record of conciliation, boundary n6 warns to check what that record covered.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text does not state the claimed exceptions to prior conciliation, continued commercial-section competence until installation, the boundary n7/n6 warnings, or a requirement to check what a conciliation record covered.

pairs.statement: A settlement is recorded in a record signed by the parties, the judge and the clerk, and filed at the registry.
Expert consultation may be used at any time, even during the conciliation procedure.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text permits consultation but does not identify it as expert consultation.

pairs.statement: If there is no reconciliation, or a spouse stays away despite the reflection period, the merits are taken up.

Before a claim is entered at the specialised commercial court, a conciliation requested by a party from its president must take place before a judge he designates; the requesting party notifies the others of the conciliation hearing date.
Every individual labour dispute goes first to the conciliation office before any court case.
Records of conciliation or agreement endorsed by the judges and filed at the registry are executory titles.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The excerpt lists these records but does not state that they are executory titles.

pairs.statement: When the mediator appointed is an association, its president names one of its members to carry out the mediation in its name and informs the judge.
The judge approves the agreement record by an order open to no appeal, and the record is an executory title.
The jurisdiction rules of the specialised commercial courts apply from the date the new courts are installed.
The mediator reports the outcome to the judge in writing and, if there is agreement, draws up a record he signs with the parties; the case returns on its set date.
The proceedings end with the end of the action, including by settlement.
Administrative conciliation is sought by the parties or proposed by the presiding judge with their consent.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The excerpt does not identify this conciliation procedure as administrative.

pairs.statement: The judge stays seized during mediation and may take any measure he deems necessary at any time.

This prior step is not required when: Paragraph 3 of article 536 مكرر 4 calls for the record of non-conciliation in case the attempt fails; where it ended in a record of conciliation, boundary n6 warns to check what that record covered.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text requires a non-conciliation record when conciliation fails, but states no exemption from the prior step and no boundary n6 warning or requirement to check a successful record's scope.

pairs.statement: The commercial section hears commercial disputes, except those reserved to the specialised commercial court.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text excludes disputes mentioned in article 536 مكرر, but does not supply that article or identify those disputes as reserved to the specialised commercial court.

pairs.statement: The judge may give the spouses time to reflect before a new attempt and order provisional measures by an order open to no appeal.
The administrative courts may conciliate in full-jurisdiction cases.
The judge hears each spouse separately, then together.
The spouses' reconciliation is recorded in a record signed by the judge, the clerk and the spouses and filed; it is an executory title.
Mediation may be renewed once for the same period, at the mediator's request and with the parties' agreement.
The judge must raise a plea of inadmissibility of his own motion when it is of public order.
The conciliation ends with a record signed by the judge, the parties and the clerk, governed by the code's rules.
The conciliation attempt is held where and when the judge thinks fit, unless a special text provides otherwise.
The judge may end the arbiters' mission of his own motion when it proves difficult; the proceedings then continue.
At the spouses' request, a family member may attend and take part in the attempt.
The order appointing the mediator states the parties' consent, the mediator's initial period and the date the case returns to the hearing.
In divorce by mutual consent the judge hears the spouses, checks their consent and attempts reconciliation where possible.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The excerpt describes hearing the spouses, checking consent and attempting reconciliation, but does not identify the proceedings as divorce by mutual consent.

pairs.statement: The mediator is bound to secrecy toward third parties.
When the dispute worsens and harm is not proven, two arbiters, one from each family, must be appointed and report within two months.
The president of the commercial section must first refer the dispute to mediation.
If the parties accept, the judge appoints a mediator to hear each side and try to bring them to a solution.
Subject to the conciliation rule, marriage is dissolved by divorce at the husband's will, by mutual consent, or at the wife's request.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The excerpt invokes article 49 without supplying its contents or identifying it as a conciliation rule.

pairs.statement: Divorce is established only by a judgment after several conciliation attempts by the judge, within no more than three (3) months from the filing of the claim.
When ordering interim measures the judge may take into account what the spouses agreed.
The code's territorial jurisdiction rules apply to the specialised commercial court.
The judge must offer mediation to the parties in every matter except family cases, labour cases and anything that may affect public order.
The commercial sections remain competent for claims filed with them before the new courts are installed.
A husband who takes his wife back during the conciliation attempt needs no new contract.
In an attachment of wages the president of the court tries to reconcile the attaching creditor and the debtor.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text says the court president attempts conciliation between two parties, but does not mention wage attachment or identify them as the attaching creditor and debtor.

pairs.statement: The clerk serves the appointment order on the parties and the mediator; the mediator tells the judge he accepts and invites the parties to a first meeting.
Conciliation attempts in a divorce claim are mandatory and held in closed session.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text makes conciliation attempts mandatory and confidential, but does not identify their context as a divorce claim.

pairs.statement: The conciliation record is an executory title as soon as it is filed at the registry.
Mediation before the commercial section does not depend on the parties' acceptance, unlike the general rule.
A reconciliation reached by the arbiters is recorded and approved by the judge by an order open to no appeal.
The judge may end the mediation at any time at the request of the mediator or the parties, or of his own motion when it cannot proceed properly; the case then returns to the hearing.
The code's general mediation rules apply to mediation before the commercial section.
A plea of inadmissibility seeks dismissal of the claim for lack of the right to sue, without examining the merits.
The ways of applying the mediator's conditions are set by regulation.
The judge may conciliate the parties during the proceedings, in any matter.
Arbitration is open for rights a person may freely dispose of, never for public-order matters or personal status and capacity.
Mediation is entrusted to a natural person or to an association.
The parties may settle on their own or at the judge's initiative, at every stage of the proceedings.
Mediation covers the whole dispute or part of it.
The judge draws up a record of the conciliation efforts and their results, signed by him, the clerk and both parties.

This prior step is not required when: The specialised commercial court's jurisdiction rules apply only from its installation, and the commercial section stays competent until then; the prior conciliation is a step before that court. This is a reading the text does not settle, so boundary n7 warns in this case.
pairs.missingOrWrong: The text does not mention prior conciliation, any exemption from it, or boundary n7. Its continued-competence rule concerns claims filed before installation, rather than expressly stating a general until-installation rule.

pairs.statement: The plaintiff in a divorce case formally serves the petition on the defendant and the prosecution, and may have the clerk's office notify the prosecution.
The judge may rule urgently, by order on petition, on interim measures, in particular maintenance, custody, visiting rights and housing.
When conciliation fails, the claim is filed by petition with the record of non-conciliation attached, on pain of inadmissibility in form.
If a spouse personally summoned fails to attend without excuse, the judge records it.
With the parties' agreement the mediator may hear any person who consents and whose hearing helps settle the dispute, and he informs the judge of the difficulties he meets.
If no harm is proven during the proceedings, the judge may appoint a pair of arbiters to attempt reconciliation under the Family Code.
An administrative court conducts conciliation only in disputes within its own jurisdiction.
The conciliation attempts may not exceed three (3) months from the filing of the divorce claim.
Mediation may not last more than three (3) months.
The mediator must be of good conduct and integrity, free of any conviction for a crime against honour, qualified, neutral and independent.
If a spouse cannot attend, the judge may set a later date or delegate another judge by rogatory commission.
